name: Pallof press
pattern: Anti-rotation: a cable or band pulls sideways while you press it straight out in front, and the trunk refuses to turn.
setup: Stand side-on to the anchor, about a step away, handle at chest height.
Hold the handle at your breastbone with both hands, feet hip width, knees soft.
Step out until the band is tight; square your hips and chest forward.

steps.text: Press the handle straight out from your chest without letting it pull you around.
Hold the arms straight for 2-5 s; breathe.
Bring the handle back to your chest slowly. Finish the set, then face the other way.

cues.cue: Chest and hips stay square; the hands stay on the midline.
cues.why: Resisting a turning force trains the obliques and deep trunk to stiffen the spine against rotation.

cues.cue: Press straight out, not toward the anchor.
cues.why: The force arm is longest with arms straight, so the press is the hardest point.

cues.cue: Narrow your stance or go standing to make it harder.
cues.why: Standing instead of kneeling and a smaller base raised the balance demand; an unstable surface raised it most.
A modest brace stiffens the trunk without breath holding.

breathing: Breathe out as you press, keep breathing during the hold.

tempo.note: Press in 2 s, hold 2-5 s, return in 2 s.

mistakes.name: Turning toward the anchor
mistakes.looks: Shoulders and hips twist toward the cable as you press.
mistakes.fix: Lighter load; keep the hands on your midline.
mistakes.why: The trunk is losing the anti-rotation fight.

mistakes.name: Leaning away
mistakes.looks: The body tilts away from the anchor to fight the pull.
mistakes.fix: Stand tall, weight even on both feet.
mistakes.why: Leaning replaces trunk work with body weight.

mistakes.name: Ribs flare, back arches
mistakes.looks: The low back arches as the arms go out.
mistakes.why: It turns into a shoulder press.

safety: Low back pain: anti-rotation work is often well tolerated; start kneeling with a light band.
Shoulder pain: keep the press below shoulder height.

variants.change: Kneeling: lower centre of mass and less balance demand.
Hold the press while squatting, stepping, bridging or doing a dead bug.
Anti-rotation chop: arms move high to low while the trunk stays square.

subtypes.name: Half-kneeling Pallof press
subtypes.change: Inside knee down, outside foot forward.

subtypes.name: Lying Pallof press or anti-rotation dead bug
subtypes.change: On your back (or in a bridge) pressing the handle to the ceiling against the side pull.

motion.basis: Anchor is on the subject's right. Angles are estimates from the technique; the convention has no trunk-rotation key, so a rotation fault is shown with hip rotation and arm drift. Difficulty ranking from juanrecio2025.
